explanation: P39 successfully corrects Bash exit semantics, removes the invalid job-scope runner.temp expression, establishes manual-only fail-closed trust anchors, preserves zero-request/zero-quota boundaries, and passes exact-head CI. One blocking two-checkout defect remains: the workflow validates the future Human Decision on the authorization-record revision, then checks out the earlier reviewed execution revision and invokes the runtime with a decision path inside that execution tree. Because the Human Decision is committed after the execution revision is selected, that file cannot exist in the earlier execution tree, so a fully bound launcher would terminate as technical-failure before every API request. The tests validate authorization in one temporary tree but do not exercise preservation of the decision record across the two checkouts. The decision JSON must be staged outside the workspace before the execution checkout and then validated and consumed using reviewed execution code without executing dependencies or repository code from the decision-record revision.
